questions.stem: The branch of geography that studies the origin, site, shape and classification of towns and cities is
explanation_steps: The textbook defines Urban Geography as 'the study of the origin, site, shape and classification of towns and cities' – the stem repeats this definition word for word.

Economic geography studies activities such as agriculture, manufacturing and mining; population geography studies the number, distribution and composition of people; biogeography studies plants and animals. Answer: D.
tips: Towns and cities → urban (Latin urbs = city).

similar_questions.stem: The branch of human geography that studies economic activities such as agriculture, manufacturing and mining is
explanation_steps: Textbook definition of economic geography.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 1 – The Subject Matter of Geography

questions.stem: Which of the following agricultural practices is dominant in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: The textbook (agriculture in Eritrea): in the main farming regions 'the type of production is mainly subsistence', and 'farming is traditional in its character and is meant for subsistence use'.

Pastoralism and animal husbandry are important, especially in the lowlands, but most rural households farm mainly to feed themselves. Commercial farming is limited to a few irrigated schemes. Answer: B.
tips: Eritrean farming = small plots, traditional tools, rain-fed, for family consumption → subsistence.

similar_questions.stem: Most Eritrean farmers cultivate crops mainly
explanation_steps: Subsistence farming = production for home use.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Days and nights are the result of the

options.D: distance between the Sun and Earth.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The daily motion of the earth around its own axis causes alternation of day and night… the earth's rotation causes the alternate change of day and night or light and dark.'
Revolution (with the tilted axis) causes the seasons and the changing length of day and night, not day and night themselves. Answer: A.
tips: Rotation = 24 hours = day and night. Revolution = 365¼ days = seasons.

similar_questions.stem: The change of seasons on the earth is caused by

options.B: revolution and the inclination of the earth's axis
options.D: the distance of the earth from the moon

explanation_steps: Revolution with a tilted axis changes the angle of the sun's rays through the year.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, dark coloured clay soils are dominantly found in the
explanation_steps: The Southern Plateau (Seraye) has a basalt surface formed by lava flows; the textbook says it is 'agriculturally rich because of its flat topography, adequate rainfall and fertile black soils'.
Basaltic soils of the lava plateau are fine-textured clays that crack when dry and become sticky when wet – the dark clay (vertisol-type) soils.
The Anseba and Eastern Highlands are mainly granite, metamorphic and sandstone terrain with thin soils; the coastal lowlands have sandy soils. Answer: E.
tips: Basalt → dark, fine clay soil. The basalt plateau is the Southern Plateau (Mendefera–Adi Quala).

similar_questions.stem: Basaltic soils in Eritrea are fine-textured because they

options.B: develop in areas with a high degree of weathering
options.D: are found only on steep slopes

explanation_steps: Textbook: basaltic soils develop where weathering is high, so they are fine-textured.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 7 – Relief and Drainage Systems in Eritrea

additional_textbook_refs.section: 5.1.1 Soils of the Highlands – basaltic soils

questions.review_flag: Textbook also lists (dark, cracking) Vertisols around Tessenei, Alighder and Golij in the western plain; if the setter meant vertisols, option C ('North-western Lowlands') is arguable. Keyed E (black soils of the Southern Plateau). Teacher decision.

questions.stem: All of the following are elements of weather and climate, <u>except</u>
explanation_steps: The textbook lists the elements of weather and climate as temperature, air pressure, wind, humidity and precipitation (plus cloud cover and sunshine).
All four named items are elements, so none is an exception. Answer: E.
tips: Elements (what we measure) ≠ controls/factors (latitude, altitude, distance from the sea).

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a factor (control) of climate rather than an element?
explanation_steps: Altitude influences the elements; it is not itself measured as weather.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The geographic distribution of elephants in Eritrea is limited to the
explanation_steps: The textbook (wildlife): 'recent studies indicate that at present there are elephants in the south-east Gash-Barka Zone' – the Gash-Setit area along the Setit river.
Buri peninsula is known for wild ass and gazelles, the Dahlak Islands and Southern Red Sea for marine life (dugong, turtles), and Semenawi Bahri for its forest. Answer: B.
tips: Elephants need water and tall vegetation → the wetter south-west (Gash-Setit).

similar_questions.stem: Which endangered animal of Eritrea lives in the Red Sea?
explanation_steps: The dugong is a marine mammal (Fig. 4.1 endangered animals).
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – Natural Vegetation and Wildlife in Eritrea

questions.stem: An anemometer is an instrument used to measure the ______ of a place.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The speed of wind is measured by an instrument called an Anemometer. The most common anemometer is the three-cup anemometer.'
Temperature – thermometer; rainfall – rain gauge; pressure – barometer; wind direction – wind vane. Answer: D.
tips: Anemos (Greek) = wind; anemometer = wind-speed meter; vane = direction.

similar_questions.stem: The instrument used to show wind direction is the
explanation_steps: The wind vane points to where the wind comes from.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following represents mechanical weathering?
explanation_steps: Mechanical (physical) weathering breaks rocks into pieces without changing their chemical composition. The textbook: when the outer layer of rocks expands and contracts with heating and cooling, 'the outer layer of the rocks is peeled off. This process is called exfoliation. This is common in hot desert areas.'
Decomposition, hydration and solution are chemical changes (chemical weathering). Answer: B.
tips: Physical = break up (exfoliation, frost action). Chemical = change (solution, oxidation, hydration, carbonation).

similar_questions.stem: Frost action (freezing and thawing of water in rock cracks) is an example of
explanation_steps: Ice expands and splits the rock – no chemical change.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 2 – Gradation by Rivers and Winds

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the developing countries?
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Less developed countries of the world have a higher percentage of their population engaged in primary activities like agriculture' – that is, most people live in rural areas.
Options A, B, C and E describe developed countries (high income, long life, low disease, industrial economies). Answer: D.
tips: Developing = low income, short life, many diseases, mostly rural farmers.

similar_questions.stem: A high percentage of the labour force employed in agriculture indicates that a country is
explanation_steps: Employment structure reflects development.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Deep ocean trenches are formed along the

options.C: collision of ocean floors with continental plates.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'When two ocean floors collide, one sinks below the other and forms a deep trench in the ocean floor.' This is the case it links to trenches (e.g. the Mariana islands).

Two continental plates do not subduct – they form fold mountains (Himalayas). In general geography, trenches also form where an ocean floor subducts beneath a continent (e.g. the Peru–Chile trench beside the Andes), so C is also defensible. Answer: A (C also accepted).
tips: Trench = subduction of an oceanic plate. Continent–continent = fold mountains only.

similar_questions.stem: The Himalayas were formed by the collision of

options.C: an ocean floor and a continental plate

explanation_steps: Indo-Australian and Eurasian (continental) plates collided.
Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: The textbook ties deep trenches to ocean–ocean collision (A), but ocean–continent subduction also forms trenches (Peru–Chile). Both accepted; teacher decision.

questions.stem: Soil is made up of a variety of natural components including
explanation_steps: The textbook (components of soil): soil consists of mineral (inorganic) matter, organic matter (humus and organisms), water and air.
All four are components. Answer: E.
tips: Soil = minerals + organic matter + water + air (roughly 45 : 5 : 25 : 25 by volume).

similar_questions.stem: The dark, decomposed organic material in soil is called
explanation_steps: Humus comes from decayed plants and animals.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The origin of an earthquake inside the crust of the earth is called
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The point inside the earth where the earthquake occurs is called the focus, while the corresponding point on the surface of the earth lying directly above the focus is known as the epicenter.'
Answer: B.
tips: Focus = underground origin; epicentre = on the surface directly above it.

similar_questions.stem: The place on the earth's surface that usually suffers the greatest damage in an earthquake is the
explanation_steps: It lies directly above the focus.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The Greek word klima refers to the
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The word climate comes from the Greek klima, which means the inclination of the sun.'
Answer: B.
tips: klima = slope/inclination – the angle of the sun's rays controls temperature.

similar_questions.stem: Climate is best defined as

options.A: the day-to-day state of the atmosphere
options.B: the average weather conditions of a place over a long period
options.C: the amount of rain in one month

explanation_steps: Climate = long-term average weather (about 30 years).
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 1 – Major Types of World Climates

questions.stem: The total amount of rainfall received in Eritrea decreases from
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Rainfall generally tends to increase from north to south' (Fig. 3.5), from under 200 mm in the north to more than 700 mm in the south-west.
If rainfall increases north → south, it decreases south → north. Answer: B.
tips: Adi Quala (687 mm) > Mendefera > Asmara > Keren > Nakfa: wetter in the south.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these highland towns receives the highest mean annual rainfall?
explanation_steps: Rainfall increases towards the south: Adi Quala 687 mm.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The average number of years a person is expected to live at birth is referred to as
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Life expectancy refers to the average number of years a person is expected to live.'
Answer: B.
tips: Life expectancy is higher in developed countries and a key part of the HDI.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following usually raises life expectancy?
explanation_steps: Fewer deaths from disease → longer lives.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The longest mountain system in southern Europe is the
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Alps: This is the longest mountain system in southern Europe. It stretches for over 1000 kilometers from east to west.'
Andes – South America; Atlas – north-west Africa; Rockies – North America; Himalayas – South Asia. Answer: A.
tips: Match each range with its continent before answering.

similar_questions.stem: The longest mountain range on the continents, stretching about 7,200 km along western South America, is the
explanation_steps: Textbook: Andes ≈ 7,200 km.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, there is high potential for large-scale irrigated agriculture in the
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The Western Lowlands have a high potential for large-scale irrigated agriculture (e.g. cereals, fruits, vegetables…)' – flat land, fertile alluvial soils and rivers such as Gash, Setit and Barka.
Answer: C.
tips: Large-scale irrigation needs flat land + big rivers + good soils → Western Lowlands.

similar_questions.stem: The only perennial river of Eritrea, useful for irrigation in the Western Lowlands, is the
explanation_steps: Setit flows throughout the year.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 7 – Relief and Drainage Systems in Eritrea

questions.stem: Which of the following factors does <u>not</u> influence the distribution of population?
explanation_steps: The textbook (factors affecting population distribution and density): physical factors include climate, relief, soils, vegetation and water supply; human factors include economic, political and social conditions.
All four listed factors influence where people live. Answer: E.
tips: Physical factors: climate, relief, soil, water, vegetation. Human factors: jobs, transport, politics, history.

similar_questions.stem: Why are the frozen lands of northern Canada sparsely populated?

options.B: Extremely cold climate and short growing season

explanation_steps: Climate discourages settlement there.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 3.3.1 Factors affecting population distribution and density

questions.stem: Which of the following factors does <u>not</u> affect the formation of soil?
explanation_steps: The textbook (formation of soil): the soil-forming factors are parent material, climate, topography (relief), living organisms and time.
All four listed options are soil-forming factors. Answer: E.
tips: Remember CLORPT: CLimate, Organisms, Relief, Parent material, Time.

similar_questions.stem: Which soil-forming factor explains why soils are thin on steep slopes?
explanation_steps: Steep slopes lose soil by erosion.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: All of the following are chief occupations of rural people, <u>except</u>
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'rural settlements have the majority of their population engaged in primary activities like farming, herding, fishing, forestry, and mining… Urban settlements have the majority of their population engaged in secondary or tertiary activities like industry, administration, health, and education.'
Administration is an urban (tertiary) occupation. Answer: A.
tips: Rural = primary activities; urban = secondary and tertiary.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a tertiary activity typical of urban settlements?
explanation_steps: Services are tertiary.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: In a sea breeze, winds blow from
explanation_steps: By day the land heats faster than the sea, so low pressure forms over the land and higher pressure over the sea. The textbook: this 'causes winds to blow from sea to land, which is known as sea breezes'. At night the land breeze blows from land to sea.
Answer: C.
tips: Winds are named after where they come FROM: sea breeze comes from the sea.

similar_questions.stem: A land breeze usually blows

options.A: during the day from sea to land
options.B: at night from land to sea
options.C: at night from sea to land
options.E: from mountains to valleys by day

explanation_steps: At night the land is cooler (high pressure).
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 2.3 Effects of revolution – land and sea

additional_textbook_refs.section: 3.6 Local winds – land and sea breezes

questions.stem: Wind erosion is more powerful in arid areas due to the

options.C: presence of loose sand and silt soils.

explanation_steps: The textbook: wind erosion is great in hot deserts because there is little vegetation to protect the surface and the ground is covered by loose, dry, fine particles (sand and silt) that the wind can easily lift.
Compact soils resist wind erosion, so D is wrong; A, B and C are all correct. Answer: E.
tips: Wind erodes best where it is dry, bare and loose.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following reduces wind erosion?
explanation_steps: Trees reduce wind speed near the ground.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 2 – Gradation by Rivers and Winds

questions.stem: Isotherms are lines drawn on a map to connect places with the same amount of
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Isotherms are lines that connect all places with the same average annual temperature.'
Rainfall – isohyets; pressure – isobars; sunshine – isohels. Answer: C.
tips: iso = equal; therm = heat.

similar_questions.stem: Lines on a map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure are called
explanation_steps: bar = pressure.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: Soils of poorly developed horizons that are mainly formed in semi-arid areas of Eritrea are
explanation_steps: The textbook (soils of the western plain): 'Xerosols: These soils develop in semi-arid areas. They have poorly developed horizons, but they may be used for cultivation with adequate supply of water.'
Regosols are immature soils from sandstone in north-west Barka; Cambisols are fertile brown loams; Vertisols are cracking clays around Tessenei. Answer: D.
tips: xero = dry → Xerosols = soils of dry (semi-arid) areas.

similar_questions.stem: In Eritrea, soils that become hard in the dry season and sticky in the rainy season, found around Tessenei and Alighder, are
explanation_steps: Vertisols: difficult to prepare, high water retention.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.section: 5.1.2 Soils of the Lowlands – western plain

questions.stem: The type of migration that takes place within the national boundary of a country is called
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Migrations that take place within a territorial limit of a country are called internal migration' (e.g. rural-to-urban migration).
External/international migration crosses national borders. Answer: A.
tips: Inside the borders = internal; across borders = international (external).

similar_questions.stem: A person who leaves Eritrea to live permanently in another country is, from Eritrea's point of view, an
explanation_steps: Emigrant = person leaving (exit).
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following does <u>not</u> contribute to desertification?
explanation_steps: The textbook (desertification): the process is driven by climatic variations (drought, climate change) and by human activities – expansion of cultivation into marginal land, over-cultivation (intensification), overgrazing and deforestation.
All four listed options contribute. Answer: E.
tips: Desertification = land degradation in drylands by climate + human misuse.

similar_questions.stem: Which practice helps to fight desertification?
explanation_steps: Vegetation cover protects the soil.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 5 – Cultural Impact on Physical Environment

questions.stem: A population pyramid that represents a large number of young people is referred to as
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Expansive: A pyramid showing rapid population growth with larger number of people of younger age' – a wide base narrowing sharply upwards.
Constrictive pyramids have a narrow base (low birth rate); stationary pyramids have similar numbers in most age groups. Answer: A.
tips: Wide base = many children = expansive (typical of developing countries such as Eritrea).

similar_questions.stem: A population pyramid with a narrow base and a wide middle, typical of countries with falling birth rates, is
explanation_steps: Fewer young people than middle-aged.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The seasonal temperature distribution in Eritrea is a function of
explanation_steps: The textbook: spatial temperature differences within Eritrea 'are caused by extreme altitude differences. The seasonal temperature distribution in Eritrea is however a function of latitude.' Between March and September the overhead sun moves north across Eritrea, bringing the hot season.
Altitude explains place-to-place differences (Asmara cool, Massawa hot); latitude explains the seasonal (time) differences. Answer: B.
tips: Where? → altitude. When (season)? → latitude (position of the overhead sun).

similar_questions.stem: Asmara is much cooler than Massawa throughout the year mainly because of differences in
explanation_steps: Spatial difference → altitude.
Answer: C.

questions.review_flag: Keyed B from the textbook sentence ('seasonal temperature distribution … is a function of latitude'); some teachers may expect E (all factors). Teacher decision.

questions.stem: A type of climate characterized mainly by clear skies and abundant sunshine is
explanation_steps: The textbook lists 'clear skies and abundant sunshine especially in summer' as one of the three distinctive characteristics of the Mediterranean climate (with winter rain and mild winters), and repeats it in the summary.

Hot deserts are also cloudless and sunny for most of the year (sub-tropical high pressure), so C is defensible on general knowledge. Monsoon, savannah and west-margin climates have cloudy rainy seasons. Answer: D (C also accepted).
tips: Textbook phrase 'clear skies and abundant sunshine' = Mediterranean summer.

similar_questions.stem: The Mediterranean climate receives most of its rainfall in
explanation_steps: Rainfall is concentrated in winter; summers are almost rainless.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 1 – Major Types of World Climates

questions.review_flag: Textbook phrase belongs to the Mediterranean climate (D), but tropical deserts are the most cloudless, sunny climate (C). Both accepted; teacher decision.

questions.stem: A continuous urban settlement created by the spread and merging of cities is called
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The process of merging or coalescence of urban settlements is called conurbation… Such places are called a megalopolis', and in the summary: 'when cities… meet, they create a continuous urban settlement called megalopolis.'

So the textbook calls the merging process conurbation and the resulting continuous settlement a megalopolis; in general usage 'conurbation' is also used for the merged urban area itself. Answer: B (E also accepted).
tips: Textbook: conurbation = the merging; megalopolis = the continuous urban region produced.

similar_questions.stem: The movement of people and activities from the city centre to the outskirts is called
explanation_steps: Growth of suburbs.
Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: Textbook: merging process = conurbation, the continuous settlement = megalopolis (B); many sources call the merged area itself a conurbation (E). Both accepted; teacher decision.

questions.stem: Which of the following map scales is the smallest?
explanation_steps: A scale is a fraction: 1:1,000,000 = 1/1,000,000, the smallest fraction of the five, so it is the smallest scale (shows a large area with little detail).
The textbook: small-scale maps 'have scales that are smaller than 1:250,000 (like 1:1,000,000)'. Answer: E.
tips: Bigger denominator → smaller scale → larger area, less detail.

similar_questions.stem: Which scale gives the most detail?
explanation_steps: Largest fraction = largest scale.
Answer: A.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 6 – Scales and Classification of Map Scales

questions.stem: Crustal plates movement and their interaction are responsible for the
explanation_steps: The textbook: plate movement is 'the main cause for the building of mountains, the development of trenches, earthquakes, volcanic activity, and more'. Rift valleys form at divergent boundaries (e.g. the East African rift).
Answer: E.
tips: Plate tectonics explains mountains, rifts, earthquakes and volcanoes together.

similar_questions.stem: The East African Rift Valley is an example of a
explanation_steps: Plates move apart there.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The weather forming process of the earth is greatly influenced by the layer of the atmosphere known as
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere found near the earth's surface', holding most of the air mass, water vapour and dust – so clouds, rain, storms and winds (weather) form there.
Answer: A.
tips: Tropo = turning/mixing: all weather happens in the troposphere.

similar_questions.stem: The ozone layer that absorbs ultraviolet radiation is found in the
explanation_steps: Ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Headlands and bays are formed by wave erosion when the coastal rocks consist of
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Headlands and bays are formed when coastal rocks consist of alternate layers of' hard and soft rock. Waves erode the soft rock quickly into bays, leaving the hard rock projecting as headlands.
Answer: B.
tips: Differential erosion: soft → bay, hard → headland.

similar_questions.stem: When a natural arch collapses, the isolated pillar of rock left standing in the sea is a
explanation_steps: Cave → arch → stack.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 – Gradation by the Action of Waves

questions.stem: An irrigated agriculture is associated with ______ economic activity.
explanation_steps: Primary activities obtain products directly from nature: agriculture (irrigated or rain-fed), herding, fishing, forestry and mining. The textbook groups 'primary activities like agriculture'.
Secondary = manufacturing; tertiary = services; quaternary = information and research. Answer: A.
tips: Irrigation is a farming method, and farming is always primary.

similar_questions.stem: A factory that processes tomatoes into tomato paste is engaged in
explanation_steps: Processing/manufacturing = secondary.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: A type of rural settlement that lasts for several months in a place is classified as
explanation_steps: The textbook classifies rural settlements by duration: ephemeral (1–7 days), temporary (1–30 days), seasonal ('if they last several months in a place'), semi-permanent (several years) and permanent (several generations).
Answer: D.
tips: Days → ephemeral; weeks → temporary; months → seasonal; years → semi-permanent; generations → permanent.

similar_questions.stem: Settlements of shifting cultivators that last several years in one place are classified as
explanation_steps: Several years = semi-permanent.
Answer: D.

questions.stem: The largest portion of ocean floors consists of
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'On the floor, there are vast flat plains called abyssal plains (deep sea plains), many ridges, mountains, hills, very deep valleys and trenches.' The abyssal (deep-sea) plains are the most extensive feature.
Answer: E.
tips: Ocean floor: continental shelf → slope → abyssal plain (most of the area) with ridges and trenches.

similar_questions.stem: The gently sloping, shallow submerged edge of a continent is the
explanation_steps: Continental shelf = submerged extension of the continent.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, trachyte hills are mainly found in the
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Trachytes are also volcanic rocks that resemble sandstone. Their cover is confined to small areas of Senafe such as the cliffs and flat-topped hills of Emba Metera, Emba Tarika, Emba Seim and Emba Kessad.'
Senafe and these peaks belong to the Eastern Highlands. Answer: D.
tips: Trachyte = Senafe area (Emba Metera etc.) = Eastern Highlands; basalt = Southern Plateau.

similar_questions.stem: The basalt covers of the interior plateau of Eritrea were formed during the
explanation_steps: Oligocene lava outpourings formed the oldest basalt and trachyte covers.
Answer: C.

additional_textbook_refs.unit: Unit 7 – Relief and Drainage Systems in Eritrea

questions.stem: The two most basic demographic characteristics of a given population are
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Age and sex are the most basic characteristics of a population.' They are shown together in the population pyramid.
Answer: D.
tips: Population pyramid = age (vertical) × sex (left/right).

similar_questions.stem: The number of males per 100 females in a population is the
explanation_steps: Sex ratio compares males and females.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, the geological structure with better amount of ground water is associated with
explanation_steps: The textbook: volcanic traps (the plateau south of Asmara, Senafe) 'contain considerable amounts of ground water', and the unconsolidated alluvial fans at the foot of the escarpments 'store water that flows from the Highlands' with a perennial sub-surface flow.
Consolidated sediments have 'poor ground water bearing characteristics', and basement rocks are impermeable. So both C and D are good aquifers. Answer: E (D alone also accepted).
tips: Good aquifers: volcanic traps and alluvial deposits. Poor: basement (crystalline) rocks and consolidated sediments.

similar_questions.stem: Most rainwater becomes run-off over basement (crystalline) rocks in Eritrea because these rocks are
explanation_steps: Impermeable rock → little infiltration.
Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: Textbook presents volcanic traps as the main aquifer but also stresses alluvial fans; keyed E, D accepted. Teacher decision.

questions.stem: The gases that make up about 99 percent of the earth's atmosphere are
explanation_steps: The textbook: nitrogen (78 %) and oxygen (21 %) – 'both nitrogen and oxygen form 99% of the total volume of the atmosphere. The remaining 1% is formed by various gases such as argon, carbon dioxide…'
Answer: A.

similar_questions.stem: Which gas makes up the largest share of the atmosphere by volume?
explanation_steps: Nitrogen ≈ 78 %.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The two principal winds that blow over Eritrea during the summer season and winter season, <u>respectively</u>, are the

options.A: northeast trade winds and south westerly winds.
options.B: northeast trade winds and south easterly winds.
options.C: southwesterly winds and northeast trade winds.
options.D: southwesterly winds and south easterly winds.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'During summer season, the dominant winds in Eritrea are the south-westerly winds' (south-east trades deflected after crossing the equator), which bring the main summer rains. In winter, when the ITCZ lies to the south, 'the north east trade winds blow from Asia and Arabia to southern Africa across Eritrea'.
Summer first, winter second → south-westerlies, then north-east trades. Answer: C.
tips: 'Respectively' – keep the order: summer (SW) then winter (NE).

similar_questions.stem: Winter rain along the Eritrean Red Sea coast is brought by the

options.B: north-east trade winds after crossing the Red Sea

explanation_steps: The NE trades pick up moisture over the Red Sea.
Answer: B.

explanation_steps: Steep low down, gentle high up = convex.

questions.stem: [Contour map, see Figure 1 (image).] The map distance between point E and point Z is 1.5 cm. What is the average gradient, in percent?

Contour interval 40 m; labelled contours 1480 (across the south-centre), 1680 (curving round point K), 1840 (just east of point Z) and 2040 (round the large flat area A). A broad flat-topped upland inside the highest closed contour occupies the north-east, with point A in its centre. Point W lies at the tip of a narrow contour tongue on the northern edge of this upland, pointing east towards higher ground. An east–west ridge crosses the middle of the map: T sits inside a small closed contour (knoll) at its western end, X at the tip of a westward contour tongue, and Z at the tip of a westward tongue on the 1800 m contour. Gradient = VI ÷ HE × 100 = 360 ÷ 4,500 × 100 = 8 %. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Write any <u>two</u> distinctive characteristics of the Mediterranean Climate. (2 points)
questions.answer: Any two of: (1) annual rainfall is concentrated in winter, while summers are almost without rain (hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters); (2) winter temperatures are unusually mild and summer temperatures are warm to hot; (3) clear skies and abundant sunshine, especially in summer.
explanation_steps: The textbook: the Mediterranean climate 'has the following three distinctive characteristics: a. Annual rainfall is concentrated entirely in winter, while summers are almost without rain. b. Winter temperatures are unusually mild and summer temperatures vary from hot to warm. c. There are clear skies and abundant sunshine especially in summer.'
Location (west sides of continents about 30°–40° N and S, around the Mediterranean Sea) may be added but is not a climatic characteristic by itself.
marking_points: 1 point each for any two: winter rain / dry summer; mild winters and warm–hot summers; clear skies and abundant sunshine in summer.
tips: The key idea is winter rain and summer drought – the reverse of most climates.

similar_questions.stem: Why do tourists prefer to visit Mediterranean lands in summer?
similar_questions.answer: Summers are dry, warm to hot and sunny with clear skies, which suits beach and outdoor holidays.
explanation_steps: Link to characteristics (a) and (c).

questions.stem: Name any <u>two</u> categories of soils based on the size of their particles. (2 points)
questions.answer: Any two of: sand (sandy soil – coarse particles), silt (silty soil – medium particles), clay (clayey soil – very fine particles). Loam, a mixture of the three, may also be credited.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Soil texture refers to the size of soil particles. Based on size of particles, there are three principal groups of soils. These are sand, silt, and clay.'
marking_points: 1 point each for any two of: sand, silt, clay (loam acceptable as a mixture).
tips: Sand is coarsest and drains fastest; clay is finest and holds most water.

similar_questions.stem: Why do clay soils hold more water than sandy soils?
similar_questions.answer: Clay particles are very fine and closely packed, giving many tiny pore spaces that hold water; sandy soils have large pores through which water drains quickly.
explanation_steps: Relate texture to porosity and permeability.

questions.stem: Give a short definition of relative humidity. (1 point)
questions.answer: Relative humidity is the ratio (expressed as a percentage) between the actual amount of water vapour in the air and the maximum amount the air could hold at that temperature.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The amount of moisture in the air compared to the amount it can hold is called relative humidity. It is the ratio between the actual amount of water vapor in the air and the total amount of water vapor the air can hold at a particular temperature.' Saturated air has a relative humidity of 100 %.
marking_points: 1 point: actual water vapour in the air compared with (as a % of) the maximum the air can hold at the same temperature.
tips: Always mention 'at that temperature' and 'percentage'.

similar_questions.stem: Air at 30 °C holds 15 g of water vapour per m³ but could hold 30 g. What is its relative humidity?
explanation_steps: RH = actual ÷ maximum × 100.

questions.stem: List down any <u>two</u> major aspects that differentiate rural settlements from urban settlements. (2 points)
questions.answer: Any two of: (1) Occupation – most rural people are engaged in primary activities (farming, herding, fishing, forestry, mining), while most urban people work in secondary and tertiary activities (industry, trade, administration, health, education); (2) Infrastructure and services – rural areas have little or no piped water, sewerage, electricity, schools and health facilities, while towns have them; (3) Functions – urban settlements perform political, administrative, social, religious and educational functions for a wider area; (4) Size and density of population – towns are generally larger and more densely built up.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Generally, rural settlements have the majority of their population engaged in primary activities… Moreover, there is little or no investment in public infrastructure… Urban settlements have the majority of their population engaged in secondary or tertiary activities… Urban settlements often perform political, social, religious, and educational functions.' It adds that 'the distinction between urban and rural is based on occupation rather than size'.
marking_points: 1 point each for any two correct contrasts: occupation (primary vs secondary/tertiary); infrastructure/services; functions; size/density (with contrast stated).
tips: State each aspect as a contrast (rural … whereas urban …).

similar_questions.stem: Why does the textbook say that size alone cannot separate rural from urban settlements?
similar_questions.answer: Because there are big villages and small towns; the main difference is the occupation of the people (primary vs secondary/tertiary) and the functions and services the settlement provides.
explanation_steps: Occupation rather than size.

questions.stem: What are the <u>two</u> variables used in the calculation of a net migration rate? (2 points)
questions.answer: (1) The number of immigrants (in-migrants) and (2) the number of emigrants (out-migrants). Net migration rate = (immigrants − emigrants) ÷ total population × 1000.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The net migration rate shows the net effect of immigration and emigration on an area's population', calculated from the difference between immigrants and emigrants per 1000 of the population.
tips: If total population is also named as the base, it can be mentioned, but the two variables are immigrants and emigrants.

similar_questions.stem: A town of 200,000 people receives 6,000 immigrants and loses 2,000 emigrants in a year. Calculate its net migration rate.
explanation_steps: Subtract out from in, divide by population, × 1000.

questions.stem: Mention the <u>three</u> factors that led to the rapid increase of world population after 1750 AD. (3 points)
questions.answer: (1) The Industrial Revolution in western Europe – new scientific discoveries enabled farmers to increase food and livestock production; (2) Development of science and technology in transport, which opened remote and vacant lands (the Americas, Australia) for settlement and resource use; (3) Availability of medical facilities, regular food distribution, housing and public sanitation, and vaccines against infectious diseases (smallpox, cholera, typhoid), which greatly reduced death rates.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The most important factors that caused a rapid population increase after 1750 are: i) The beginning of the Industrial Revolution in western Europe… ii) The development of science and technology in transportation… iii) Availability of medical facilities, regular food distribution, housing provisions, and public sanitation greatly reduced the number of deaths over births.'
marking_points: 1 point: Industrial Revolution / scientific advances raising food production
1 point: transport development opening new lands for settlement
1 point: medical care, sanitation, food distribution, vaccination lowering death rates
tips: The common thread: death rates fell while birth rates stayed high.

similar_questions.stem: Why did world population grow very slowly before 1750?
similar_questions.answer: High birth rates were cancelled out by high death rates – high infant mortality, short life expectancy, periodic famines, epidemics and under-nourishment.
explanation_steps: Textbook: population growth before 1750 was slow because of high death rates.

questions.stem: What are the <u>two</u> major water resource problems in the Highlands of Eritrea? (2 points)
questions.answer: (1) Ground water is easily depleted because of heavy pumping for irrigation; (2) siltation is a serious problem in surface water development (reservoirs and dams fill with silt).
explanation_steps: The textbook (water resource zones – the Eritrean Highlands): 'Problems of Water Resource… (a) Groundwater is easily depleted due to heavy pumping for irrigation. (b) Siltation is a serious problem in the surface water development.'
marking_points: 1 point: depletion of ground water by heavy pumping for irrigation
1 point: siltation of surface water developments (dams/reservoirs)
tips: One problem is underground (depletion), the other on the surface (siltation).

similar_questions.stem: Suggest two methods recommended by the textbook for developing water resources in the Eritrean Highlands.
similar_questions.answer: Any two of: dug wells, boreholes, river diversion, small-scale dams, and cisterns to collect roof water or water at the foot of steep slopes.
explanation_steps: Textbook: water resource development in the Highlands.

questions.stem: What are the <u>two</u> main rivers that drain into the Danakil Depression? (1 point)
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The two main rivers in this drainage system are Dandero and Endeli. Dandero originates from Soira plateau and drains into the Danakil Depression. Endeli originates from the area south of Senafe. It flows east and finally drains into Bada Depression.'
marking_points: 1 point for both: Dandero and Endeli (½ point each).
tips: Both rise in the Eastern Highlands (Soira plateau, south of Senafe).

similar_questions.stem: Why do many rivers draining into the Danakil Depression never reach the sea?
similar_questions.answer: The depression is an inland basin below sea level, and the rivers are seasonal and dry up in the sandy surface under very high evaporation, forming only seasonal lakes.
explanation_steps: Textbook: many of these rivers dry up in the sandy surface.

questions.stem: List down <u>four</u> possible alternative energy sources in Eritrea. (2 points)
questions.answer: Any four of: solar energy, wind energy, geothermal energy, biogas (biomass). Hydro-electric power (small dams) may also be credited.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Alternative sources of energy are concerned with renewable resources… Solar, wind, geothermal, and biogas are examples of alternative energy sources.' Eritrea has high sunshine, strong coastal winds (e.g. Assab) and geothermal potential in the rift (Alid).
marking_points: ½ point each for any four: solar, wind, geothermal, biogas/biomass (hydro-power acceptable).
tips: Alternative = renewable, not fuel-wood or petroleum.

similar_questions.stem: Why does Eritrea have high potential for geothermal energy?
similar_questions.answer: It lies along the Red Sea / East African rift zone with recent volcanic activity and hot springs (e.g. the Alid area), where underground heat is close to the surface.
explanation_steps: Link geothermal energy to the rift and volcanic activity.

questions.stem: Most earthquakes and volcanic activities are confined along plate boundaries. List down the <u>three</u> major belts where such activities occur. (3 points)
questions.answer: (1) The Pacific Ring of Fire (Circum-Pacific belt); (2) the Alpine–Himalayan (Mediterranean–Asiatic) belt; (3) the Mid-Atlantic Oceanic Ridge.
explanation_steps: The textbook: the major zones of volcanoes and earthquakes 'are the Pacific ring of fire, the Alpine-Himalayan Belt, and the Mid-Atlantic Oceanic Ridge (See fig. 1.15)'.
tips: Two belts are at convergent boundaries (Pacific rim, Alpine–Himalayan) and one at a divergent boundary (Mid-Atlantic).

similar_questions.stem: Why are volcanoes common around the Pacific Ocean?
similar_questions.answer: The Pacific plate and neighbouring oceanic plates subduct beneath surrounding plates; the sinking plate melts and the magma rises to form volcanoes, with strong earthquakes along the subduction zones.
explanation_steps: Subduction → magma → volcanoes and earthquakes.
